chunks: Aḥmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Ibn Qiyāmā al-Wāsiṭī — and he was from the Wāqifiyyah — who said:

I entered upon ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام and said to him, "Can there be two Imams?" He said, "No, except that one of them is silent." So I said to him, "Here you are, and there is no silent one for you," and Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام had not yet been born to him. So he said to me, "By Allah, Allah will surely bring forth from me that by which He will establish the truth and its people, and obliterate falsehood and its people."

Then after a year, Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was born to him. It was then said to Ibn Qiyāmā, "Will this sign not satisfy you?" He said, "Indeed, by Allah, it is surely a tremendous sign, but how am I to deal with what Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said regarding his son?"

key_terms.آيَةٌ: a sign or proof from Allah
key_terms.إِمَامَانِ: two Imams existing at the same time
key_terms.الْبَاطِلَ: falsehood, meaning the invalid claim and its adherents
key_terms.الْحَقَّ: the truth, meaning the true divine authority and its rightful followers
key_terms.الْوَاقِفَةِ: the Wāqifiyyah, a sect that stopped at a previous Imam and denied the subsequent Imam
key_terms.صَامِتٌ: silent; one who does not outwardly exercise the office while another Imam is manifest

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith present the birth of Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام as a proof of Imamate?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns the proof of the Imamate of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام and the emergence of his successor, Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. It presents the birth of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام as a divine sign through which the truth and its people are established and falsehood and its people are effaced, while also reflecting the hesitation of a Wāqifī narrator despite witnessing that sign.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ibn Qiyama Al Wasity, and he was from the Waqifiites who said,

‘I went over to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Musa Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, and I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can there happen to be two Imams<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, except that one of the two would be silent’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘It is that. You<sup>asws</sup> are such that there isn’t a silent one for you<sup>asws</sup>’. And there had not happened the birth of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> for him<sup>asws</sup> yet. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be Making from me<sup>asws</sup> what the Truth and its people would be affirmed by and the falsehood and its people would be obliterated by’.

So there came for him<sup>asws</sup>, after a year, Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>. So it was said to Ibn Qiyama (the narrator), ‘Does this sign not suffice for you?’ So he said, ‘But, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, it is a great sign, but how shall I deal with what Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said regarding his<sup>asws</sup> son?’
en.sarwar: 11. Ahmad ibn Mihran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from ibn Qiyama al-Wasiti who was a member of the waqifa, sect has said the following.

“Once I went to see Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.) and I said to him, “Can there be two Imams (at the same time)?” He said, “No, except if one of them would be silent.” I then said, “What about your self? There is no silent Imam with you.” His son, abu Ja’far (a.s.) was not yet born. He said, “By Allah, Allah will create from me someone to establish the truth and the people of truth and banish falsehood and the people of falsehood.”

After a year therefrom abu Ja’far (a.s.) was born. It was said to ibn Qiyama, “Does this sign not convince you?” He then said, “By Allah, the sign is great but what would I say about the words of abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about his son.”
